title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typed page numbered '- 19 -' and appears upside down in the scan. It has nothing to do with the handwritten motivic material on the neighbouring pages, which deals with commutativity constraints on Picard categories of special (O,O)-bimodules. It is almost certainly reused scrap paper: the verso of an earlier typescript on analytic functions of several complex variables.

The problem it serves: find q power series u_i(x_1,…,x_p) with no constant term that satisfy a functional system (5). From the shape of (6), (5) reads u_i = h_{i0}(x) + Σ_{|n|≥2} h_{i;n_1…n_q}(x) u_1^{n_1}…u_q^{n_q}, with the h's convergent near 0. This is the standard set-up for an analytic implicit-function or fixed-point theorem.

The argument proceeds in four steps.
1. A corollary of an earlier 'th.2' says any system of convergent series without constant term can be substituted into the convergent series Σ h_{i;n} y^n.
2. If a solution exists, both sides of (5) are therefore convergent near 0, so their coefficients must agree.
3. Write c_i(n;r) for the coefficients of h_{i;n}, c_i(r) for those of h_{i0}, and d_i(m) for those of u_i. Equating coefficients gives the system (6): d_i(0)=0 and d_i(m) = c_i(m) + Σ c_i(n;r) Π_j Π_{k≤n_j} d_j(t_{kj·}). The sum runs over r, n and t with |t_{kj}|≥1, |n|≥2, and the index balance m_l = r_l + Σ_{j,k} t_{kjl} (7).
4. Summing (7) over l shows each multi-index t_{kj} occurring on the right has total degree strictly below |m|. So by induction on the total degree s, (6) determines the coefficients of u uniquely.

This is the uniqueness and formal-existence half of Cauchy's method of undetermined coefficients. Convergence would presumably follow by majorant series on the next typed page, which is not provided.
errors: No mathematical error in the argument as typed.

Implicit hypotheses: h_{i0}(0)=0 (that is, c_i(0,…,0)=0), and (5) contains no terms linear in u, which is the condition Σ n_j ≥ 2. Both are presumably part of the statement of (5) on the previous typed page, which is not provided.
The strict inequality |t_{kj}| < |m| needs both conditions together: at least two factors are present, and each has degree ≥1. The text states this correctly.

ideas.what: Determining the coefficients of a power-series solution of an analytic functional (implicit) system by equating coefficients and inducting on total degree.
ideas.modern_name: Method of undetermined coefficients; formal uniqueness step of the analytic implicit function theorem (Cauchy–Kovalevskaya-style majorant method).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (19th century); standard textbook material (e.g. Goursat).
ideas.where_published: Unsure whether this typescript is by Grothendieck at all; it reads like a course or thesis text on analytic functions, reused as scrap paper.

ideas.what: Substitutability of convergent power series without constant term into convergent power series ('cor. du th.2').

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused upside-down typescript of a classical argument on power-series substitution and implicit analytic systems. It is unrelated to the motivic notes around it and contains only textbook material.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down (rotated 180°); it is a typed page numbered '- 19 -', not a handwritten note. The '96' in the corner is archival foliation.

The summation index in (6) is better read as ranging over (n_j), (r_l) and (t_{kjl}). It is typed as a superscript Σ^{(n_j)(t_i)}; the transcription renders this, but the t subscript is ambiguous in the image.
'a-voir' in the source is a typing hyphen; the word is 'avoir'.
